title: Which new primes create a prescribed Fekete factor?
summary: For a fixed squarefree modulus and cyclotomic order, adjoining one prime is governed exactly by the stabilizer of one cyclotomic-field value.
scope: Let \(N>1\) be squarefree, \(d\ge2\) with \(d\nmid N\), and let \(p\) be a prime not dividing \(Nd\). This concerns the principal-character Fekete polynomial.

edges.label: Möbius divisor sum
edges.explanation: Divide by 1−Xᴺ and use Proposition 2.17 to express Rₙ as a sum over divisors of N.

edges.label: Evaluate at ζ_d
edges.explanation: The assumption d∤N makes evaluation regular; the recent preprint gives explicit small-field evaluations and a broader sufficient framework.

edges.label: Field generated by the value
edges.explanation: The value α defines the intermediate field K=ℚ(α).

edges.label: Prime-extension recurrence
edges.explanation: The published recurrence Rₙₚ(X)=Rₙ(X)−Rₙ(Xᵖ), together with σₚ(ζ_d)=ζ_dᵖ, gives the displayed equality.

edges.label: Test vanishing
edges.explanation: The equality reduces the desired vanishing test to comparing α with its conjugate.

edges.label: Difference equals zero
edges.explanation: The value Rₙₚ(ζ_d) vanishes exactly when σₚ(α)=α.

edges.label: Fix a generator of K
edges.explanation: An automorphism fixing ℚ fixes α exactly when it fixes every element of ℚ(α).

edges.label: Compute the stabilizer
edges.explanation: The intermediate field determines the subgroup against which the residue class of p is tested.

edges.label: Denominator is nonzero
edges.explanation: Since d∤Np, the denominator 1−ζ_dᴺᵖ is nonzero; vanishing is equivalent to Φ_d dividing Fₙₚ over ℚ.

sources.note: Published recurrence and Möbius formula. The exact fixed-field equivalence is the elementary consequence proved below.
Automorphisms fixing an intermediate field and compatibility with rational-coefficient evaluation.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.1 and proof, pp. 17–18; Theorem 4.5, pp. 20–21; arXiv:2606.02324v1
sources.note: 2026 preprint: the explicit small-field example and a broader sufficient criterion. The general theorem is not needed for the proved equivalence on this page.

body:
This is an elementary corollary of the published recurrence, proved below. Define

\[F_N(X)=\sum_{\substack{1\le a\le N\\(a,N)=1}}X^a,\qquad R_N(X)=\frac{F_N(X)}{1-X^N}=\sum_{k\mid N}\mu(k)\frac{X^k}{1-X^k}.\]

For a primitive \(d\)-th root \(\zeta_d\), put \(\alpha=R_N(\zeta_d)\), \(L=\mathbb Q(\zeta_d)\), and \(K=\mathbb Q(\alpha)\). Let \(\sigma_p\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)\) send \(\zeta_d\) to \(\zeta_d^p\). Then the complete one-prime-extension criterion is

\[\boxed{\Phi_d\mid F_{Np}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sigma_p(\alpha)=\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sigma_p\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K).}\]

Proof. The published recurrence gives \(R_{Np}(X)=R_N(X)-R_N(X^p)\). Rational coefficients imply \(R_N(\zeta_d^p)=\sigma_p(\alpha)\). Since \(d\nmid N\) and \(p\nmid d\), both denominators \(1-\zeta_d^N\) and \(1-\zeta_d^{Np}\) are nonzero. Evaluating the recurrence proves the first equivalence; fixing a field generator proves the second.

For \(N=21,d=24\), exact arithmetic gives \(R_{21}(\zeta_{24})=\zeta_{24}^6=i\). Thus \(K=\mathbb Q(i)\) has degree two, whereas \([L:\mathbb Q]=8\), and for every prime \(p\nmid42\),

\[\Phi_{24}\mid F_{21p}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\equiv1\pmod4.\]

The 2026 preprint presents this small-field mechanism in a broader framework. Here the recurrence, field argument, and example are checked directly. The criterion decides this extension problem exactly; it does not classify every cyclotomic factor for arbitrary moduli or prove irreducibility of the noncyclotomic remainder.

title: How can exponent geometry prove absolute irreducibility?
summary: A polynomial factorization forces a Minkowski sum of lattice polytopes. If the support cannot decompose and monomial factors are excluded, no factorization survives over any field extension.
scope: Let \(k\) be any field and \(f\in k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]\) be nonconstant. Write \(P=\operatorname{Newt}(f)\) for the convex hull of its exponent vectors.

nodes.label: Any factorization over k̄: f = gh

edges.label: Ostrowski product formula
edges.explanation: The Newton polytope of a product is the Minkowski sum of the factor polytopes, also over the algebraic closure.

edges.label: Gcd of vertex differences
edges.explanation: For a lattice triangle with vertices v₀,v₁,v₂, gcd of all coordinates of v₀−v₁ and v₀−v₂ equal to one implies integral indecomposability.

edges.label: A lattice decomposition
edges.explanation: Every hypothetical factorization supplies this decomposition of P.

edges.label: No nontrivial decomposition
edges.explanation: Integral indecomposability forces a point summand in every such decomposition.

edges.label: A point summand
edges.explanation: A point Newton polytope means that the corresponding nonzero factor has exactly one monomial.

edges.label: A monomial factor
edges.explanation: This reduces every hypothetical factorization to one with a monomial factor.

edges.label: Exclude variable factors
edges.explanation: A nonconstant monomial divisor would contain at least one variable as a divisor.

edges.label: The monomial is a unit
edges.explanation: Every factorization over the algebraic closure has a constant factor, which is exactly absolute irreducibility.

sources.locator: §2.1, Lemma 1 and Corollary 2, p. 5 of arXiv:math/0012099v1
sources.note: Product formula attributed to Ostrowski; absolute-irreducibility criterion explicitly excludes variable divisors.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2; restated as Gao–Lauder, Theorem 7, p. 8 of arXiv:math/0012099v1
sources.note: The pyramid criterion specializes to the exact gcd criterion for triangles; the linked primary restatement supplies the complete statement.

body:
A lattice polytope is integrally indecomposable if every Minkowski decomposition into lattice polytopes has a point as one summand. If \(P\) has this property and no variable divides \(f\), then \(f\) is absolutely irreducible. The diagram proves this over \(\overline k\); no characteristic restriction is needed. A nonzero constant term suffices to exclude variable divisors.

For a lattice triangle \(\operatorname{conv}(v_0,v_1,v_2)\), indecomposability is equivalent to

\[\gcd\bigl(\text{all coordinates of }v_0-v_1\text{ and }v_0-v_2\bigr)=1.\]

For example, for every field \(k\) and every \(\lambda\in k\),

\[1+X^2+Y^3+\lambda XY\]

is absolutely irreducible: its vertices are \((0,0),(2,0),(0,3)\), the extra exponent \((1,1)\) lies inside the triangle, and \(\gcd(2,3)=1\). More generally, arbitrary interior coefficients are allowed whenever the three vertex coefficients remain nonzero.

The arrow has no converse: a decomposable support may still carry an irreducible polynomial. Also, \(X(1+X+Y)\) has an indecomposable translated triangle but is reducible; excluding monomial factors is essential.
